alt: Microwaves cause internal heating of body cells and infrared causes skin burns: both harm by heating. Ultraviolet damages surface cells and eyes, leading to skin cancer and eye conditions. X-rays and gamma rays cause mutation or damage to cells inside the body.
caption: Lower frequencies harm by heating; ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays damage cells directly.

alt: A radio wave of 100 MHz has wavelength 3.0 × 10⁸ / (100 × 10⁶) = 3.0 m. A 2.45 GHz microwave has wavelength 3.0 × 10⁸ / (2.45 × 10⁹) = 0.122 m, about 12 cm. All electromagnetic waves travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
caption: With the speed fixed, frequency and wavelength change in opposite directions.

alt: Plan view of the Earth with a low orbit satellite close in and a geostationary satellite much further out, orbiting once every 24 hours above the equator in the direction the Earth rotates. For a geostationary satellite 3.6 × 10⁷ m up, a signal up and back down travels 7.2 × 10⁷ m and takes 7.2 × 10⁷ / 3.0 × 10⁸ = 0.24 s.
caption: Geostationary satellites stay over one point; low orbit satellites are closer but need a network.

alt: An analogue signal varies continuously; after travelling it is weaker and noisy, and amplifying it amplifies the noise too. A digital signal has only two values; after travelling it is weak and noisy, but it can be regenerated as clean 1s and 0s because the receiver only decides between two values.
caption: Digital signals can be regenerated, so noise is removed and range increases.
